Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-18 15:30 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Ibrahim Noor (CTO, Novablend), Mina Alvarez (Head of Search), Josh Reid (Platform)

Summary (auto): Novablend needs a pilot to evaluate retrieval quality and cost. Interested in Redwood hosted for quick test, Dedicated for steady throughput, and Private VPC for sensitive customer corp data. Next steps include dataset handoff and benchmark run.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intro from our side — i'm samir, i'm the AE here at Redwood Inference, and with me is laura, our solutions eng.
[00:08] Ibrahim: thanks, yeah i'm ibrahim, CTO at novablend, mina and josh are with me — we'll be the main stakeholders.
[00:15] Mina: hi all, super excited, we run most of our search stack on a mix of ES + a vector store, looking to move densers rerank into a hosted flow.
[00:25] Laura: cool, quick clarifying q first: when you say "dense rerank" do you mean run a separate transformer reranker post recall or you want to do a single unified embedding score?
[00:33] Mina: today we do lexical recall w/ ES + a small ANN layer (we're on milvus in prod), then a transformer rerank for top 100. that's pretty expensive and introduces tail latency, so we're exploring offloading embeddings and rerank to a managed infra.
[00:45] Josh: for numbers, our traffic pattern is roughly 200 qps steady for read/search with 3x spikes on marketing events. per query we usually fanout to 10k docs at recall stage then ANN topk 500 then rerank top 100.
[01:05] Samir: that fanout's helpful — two quick levers are: 1) reduce recall fanout via smarter candidate selection (hybrid recall), 2) stage rerank cascade so heavy transformer only sees top 50. also we can help with prefix / KV caching to reduce repeated token costs.
[01:29] Ibrahim: how do you handle dimensionality choices? we've seen 768 vs 1,536 and the vec db costs scale a lot.
[01:37] Laura: right — lower dims reduce index size and ANN latency but may degrade recall depending on your domain. we typically suggest experimenting with 768 and 1,024 for text + code mixes; for long-form search or semantically subtle corpora 1,536 can help. for pilot we'll run triage: generate embeddings at three dims and measure nearest-neighbor recall and rerank delta.
[01:58] Mina: ok, can you run all three inside your hosted stack or do we need dedicated?
[02:04] Samir: we can run the pilot on hosted for faster time-to-value; if you need predictable latency or higher sustained throughput we recommend Dedicated. if data residency / encryption is required then Private (VPC) with KMS is the path. many customers start hosted for eval then move to Dedicated/Private.
[02:27] Josh: for private, do you support customer-managed keys and audit logs?
[02:31] Laura: yes — customer KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, full audit exports — i'll share the security deck. also SOC2 details.
[02:40] Ibrahim: our compliance team will want end-to-end docs, so please include retention and redaction controls.
[02:45] Samir: noted.
[02:48] Mina: what's your recommendation on hybrid search routing? we have a small taxonomy metadata filter, then dense+lexical combined.
[02:56] Laura: hybrid routing works well; one pattern is to apply metadata filters first (reduce candidate universe), then run a dense ANN for broad recall, then dedicated rerank. another is to route low-latency queries to a quantized model variant and high-cost queries to full-precision on Dedicated. Redwood supports policy-based routing and automatic fallbacks — in practice you can set cost/latency thresholds per route.
[03:22] Ibrahim: any gotchas about vector DB integration? we're on Milvus but also evaluating migrating parts to pinecone for ops simplicity.
[03:30] Laura: integrations are straightforward — we can push embeddings to your vector DB (Milvus/FAISS/pinecone/weaviate). common issues: index config mismatch (metric type/ef/nbits), shard placement, and hot-spotting during heavy fanout. we recommend sharded ANN with hedging and a fallback to a smaller topk from a cached prefix for tail cases.
[03:55] Josh: curious about rerank latency — in our perf budget we need p95 under 250ms for the whole pipeline. is that achievable?
[04:03] Samir: yes with the right tradeoffs. for example: ANN recall + small reranker (quantized) can hit p95 ~180-220ms on Dedicated. hosted can vary slightly higher; caching reduces repeated costs. We'll include latency projections in the benchmark results.
[04:20] Mina: cost question, if we do a 3-stage pipeline (recall ANN -> cheap dense score -> full transformer rerank top50), how should we think about pricing? per token for the rerank, plus embedding ops?
[04:32] Laura: correct — pricing is a combo: embedding generation cost (if done in Redwood), per-token cost for rerank invocations, and egress/storage for saved vectors. For Dedicated you can move to reserved GPU capacity which changes the unit economics. Samir will send a modeled estimate.
[04:51] Ibrahim: for benchmarking, can Redwood run the rerank stage co-located with the vector DB or does it always live in Redwood runtime?
[04:59] Laura: we can do both in the pilot: run the reranker on Redwood runtime and push embeddings to your Milvus. Alternatively, for Private deployments we can co-locate compute in your VPC so traffic stays inside. for the bench we'll test three configs: (1) hosted runtime + external Milvus, (2) hosted runtime + Redwood-managed vectors, (3) Dedicated/Private co-located option.
[05:23] Mina: good. about data residency, some of our EU customers require data to stay in EU, do you have region controls?
[05:29] Samir: yes region pinning is supported on Dedicated/Private. hosted also has EU regions but Dedicated gives stronger SLAs and isolation.
[05:36] Josh: any thoughts on embedding update patterns? we re-index nightly and sometimes do micro-update streams.
[05:42] Laura: incremental updates are supported; we recommend a hybrid approach: stream small updates to ANN, run a nightly full reindex to rebalance shards. We'll include recommended indexing cadence in the benchmark report.
[05:55] Ibrahim: what would success look like for this pilot?
[06:00] Mina: target: maintain or improve NDCG@10, reduce median latency by 20% vs current, and show predictable unit costs.
[06:08] Samir: solid goals. we'll center the pilot on those metrics. proposed timeline: dataset handoff this week, bench next week, 2-week pilot, then decision on Dedicated/Private.
[06:18] (brief cross talk)
[06:20] Josh: small question — when you say "quantized reranker" what's the model family?
[06:25] Laura: typically we test a distilled transformer quantized to int8/4 depending on accuracy hit. we also evaluate smaller siamese models for cheap dense scoring.
[06:34] Ibrahim: competitors asked — we've also talked to pinecone and weaviate, any differentiator from redwood?
[06:40] Samir: Redwood differentiates on unified runtime + routing controls and strong ops for production inference: batching, KV caching, and fallbacks. plus we offer Dedicated/Private with model variant routing; if you need fine-grained SLOs that helps.
[06:55] Mina: ok let's talk logistics for dataset: we'll share 50k doc sample and 5k canonical queries. who will own the bench run?
[07:02] Samir: Redwood will own the bench run but we need read access to your sample S3 bucket or a temporary transfer. laura will equip a notebook and metrics dashboard.
[07:13] Ibrahim: please include per-route cost estimates in the deliverable.
[07:16] Samir: yes.
[07:18] Mina: anything else?
[07:20] Laura: i'll add a short checklist in the follow-up: dataset format, expected query distribution, and preferred vector index configs.
[07:27] (wrap up)
[07:28] Samir: recap of next steps: 1) Ibrahim to upload sample dataset and grant access, 2) Samir to send pricing/bench plan, 3) laura to prepare bench checklist and notebook, 4) schedule infra deep-dive next week.
[07:45] Ibrahim: thanks, talk soon.
[07:47] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
